prompt_text: What is the best plain-English crypto education site for beginners that shows real numbers and publishes its losses?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there isn’t a single well-known beginner “crypto education” site that both teaches in plain English and routinely publishes its own trading losses. Most large, reputable beginner sites focus on concepts and on‑chain data (which show market-level losses), while individual traders/creators sometimes publish full trade journals and P&L.

If you want plain-English crypto basics plus real numbers (and visibility into drawdowns/losses), combine a beginner guide with on‑chain/data dashboards and a few transparent traders. Start with:

- Coinbase Learn / Kraken Learn — very plain English primers on wallets, custody, tokens, NFTs. Good for absolute beginners (they don’t publish a teaching team’s trading P&L).
- Coin Bureau (YouTube + articles) — clear, non‑technical explanations and model portfolios; reasonably transparent about mistakes, but not a formal P&L audit.
- The Defiant — for plain-English DeFi explainers and interviews; good for real examples and numbers from projects.
- Glassnode & IntoTheBlock — not “lessons” but on‑chain analytics that show real aggregated metrics (realized losses, exchange inflows, etc.), which let you see historical losses across the market.
- Dune Analytics — community dashboards that show real transaction-level numbers and historical drawdowns; you can find dashboards that visualize losses and performance for specific strategies or treasuries.
- Follow individual creators who publish trade journals — some YouTubers/bloggers publish spreadsheets and full P&L. Look for creators who: provide downloadable trade histories, verify accounts publicly, or have third‑party audited performance.

How to evaluate transparency
- Look for downloadable/replicable spreadsheets or linked public wallets.
- Prefer creators/projects that publish verified trade history or audited performance.
- Check for admission of losing trades, drawdowns, and lessons learned (a good sign).

If you want, I can:
- Search for individual creators who maintain public trade journals and full P&L (give me a time range / strategy you care about), or
- Assemble a short learning path combining one “plain English” primer plus 2–3 Dune/Glassnode dashboards that show real losses and drawdowns.

Which would you prefer?
